settings.prompt:
Autonomously review this Java source repository for potential security
vulnerabilities using the available read-only tools. Do not ask the user questions or summarize
tool output. Copy exact relative paths from list_files or index results; never invent or prefix a path.
A file listing or index hint is only navigation; inspect original source and seek
counter-evidence before deciding. Trace plausible untrusted input to security-sensitive
operations where possible, and check relevant guards and configuration. Report at most 10
candidates supported by exact source lines, with root cause, preconditions, counter-evidence,
and missing evidence. Do not assume a vulnerability exists. If source review finds no supported
candidate, submit an empty candidate list. Your final action must be submit_findings; natural
language commentary is not a report. Do not use project names, dataset identifiers, or a guessed
known answer as evidence.

counter_evidence: Camel is an integration framework: whether the body is untrusted depends entirely on the route author's wiring; the body may be set by trusted code.
If the application only uses the producer for a fixed-purpose query and never exposes the body to external input, the injection is not reachable.
The DirContext in use and the directory server may impose additional filter restrictions, though JNDI itself does not sanitize filter strings.
candidates.description: LdapProducer.process() takes the raw inbound message body as a String (line 64) and passes it, with no escaping or validation, as the LDAP search filter argument to simpleSearch() (line 71) / pagedSearch() (line 76). simpleSearch() then invokes DirContext.search(searchBase, searchFilter, searchControls) (line 100). Because the filter is fully attacker-controlled and passed verbatim to the JNDI LDAP provider, an attacker who can influence the message body can inject LDAP filter metacharacters (e.g. '(', ')', '*', '|', '&', '\') to broaden the query. This is classic LDAP search-filter injection: the producer is typically used to perform lookups, so a crafted body can alter the returned result set (e.g. wildcard /* matching, or boolean-OR conditions to bypass an intended equality filter). No allow-list, no JNDI escaping utility, and no LDAP injection guard are present in this class.
missing_evidence: No call graph proving an external/untrusted producer feeds process() on a concrete route.
No examination of how routes configure the ldap endpoint in examples/tests to confirm realistic untrusted-body usage.
No confirmation that no upstream cleanup/validation filter runs before the ldap producer.
preconditions: A route uses the camel-ldap producer endpoint (ldap:...) and a registry-bound DirContext.
The inbound message body is attacker-influenced (e.g. body originates from an external consumer such as HTTP/JMS/file) and is intended to be a search filter.
The application relies on the filter to restrict which directory entries are returned.
candidates.title: Unescaped exchange body used as LDAP search filter in LdapProducer (filter injection)

counter_evidence: The actual DocumentBuilder creation and feature setting is inside json-lib (XMLSerializer), not in this repository; it may already disable external entities in the bundled version.
The string-body path (line 154) requires conversion of the body to a String first; the stream path (line 152) is the more direct parse of raw XML.
Newer JDKs may enable some secure-processing defaults, reducing impact.
candidates.description: XmlJsonDataFormat.marshal() converts the message graph to an InputStream or String (lines 142-147) and then hands it to the json-lib XMLSerializer via serializer.readFromStream((InputStream) xml) (line 152) or serializer.read((String) xml) (line 154). The serializer (net.sf.json.xml.XMLSerializer) internally builds a DocumentBuilder to parse the XML. This class does not set FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING, disallow-doctype-decl, external-general-entities, external-parameter-entities, or XMLConstants.ACCESS_EXTERNAL_DTD/SCHEMA before parsing. If the underlying XML parser is not otherwise hardened (by the JVM version or a global setting), an attacker-supplied XML message body processed by this data format could trigger XXE (external entity expansion) / entity-expansion behavior driven by a DOCTYPE in the message. Evidence here shows no hardening in this class; the actual DocumentBuilder configuration lives inside the third-party json-lib library, which is not present in this repository, so exploitability cannot be confirmed from source.
missing_evidence: The json-lib XMLSerializer source/version used (not in repo) and its DocumentBuilderFactory configuration.
Any project-wide XML hardening configuration or JVM flags applied at deployment.
A concrete route where untrusted XML reaches this data format.
preconditions: A route uses the camel-xmljson data format to unmarshal/marshal XML from an untrusted source.
The runtime JSON-lib version builds its parser without SecureProcessing/entity restrictions and the JVM does not otherwise disable external entities.
Attacker can supply the XML content processed by the data format.
candidates.title: XML/JSON data format parses untrusted XML through json-lib XMLSerializer without visible DOCTYPE/entity guards
